summary: Tested merchant sign-up requests, set-password links and shop review requests on backend and frontend. Backend: 31/31 pytest tests pass (tests/test_signup_review_requests.py, -n0). Covered: signup validation (400 for missing names or bad email); duplicate pending email or existing account returns ok without creating a doc; 429 on the 6th request per IP per hour; admin list 401/403; approve creates the merchant and user with pw_nonce, email_status 'sent'; approving again returns 400, unknown id 404, existing email 409; decline works and declining again returns 404. Set-password: GET info, wrong nonce 400, wrong purpose 401, short password 400, success returns a session with no pw_nonce, login with the new password works, reusing the link returns 400. Review requests: send/list, public GET, bad tokens 401/404, a review token cannot be used as a session, empty quote 400, submit creates a hidden from_shop testimonial, a second submit returns 400, PUT publishes it to the public list. Frontend (390px): both landing CTAs go to /sign-up; the form submits (signup-done) and a bad email shows signup-error. Admin sign-up requests: approve shows the 'SET-PASSWORD EMAIL SENT' toast and the request moves to DECIDED; decline works. Admin reviews: pick mer-1, send -> 'REVIEW LINK EMAILED' toast and the request is listed. /review/{token}: submit shows thanks, reopening shows thanks, a bad token shows review-link-error. The admin sees the 'needs approval' pill and can publish. /set-password/{token}: mismatch error, success lands on /merchant/{id}, the reused and bad links show set-password-link-error. ONE REAL FAILURE: the admin notification emails are rejected by the email provider (422 undeliverable_recipient for admin@dashlocal.app).

critical.issue: Admin notification emails are never delivered. notify_admin sends to ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL or ADMIN_EMAIL (admin@dashlocal.app), and the Emergent email provider rejects it: 422 {"code":"undeliverable_recipient","message":"...For testing, send to delivered@resend.dev"}. Backend log shows 'Admin notify failed: Email provider error 422'. The user asked for the admin to be notified by email, so that part does not work. The panel listing still works.

minor.issue: The projection only excludes password_hash. For an approved store that has not set its password yet, accounts[].pw_nonce is returned to the admin client. Exclude pw_nonce (and pin_hash) there, and in current_user/auth_me.
The response user has no merchant_name, unlike /auth/login. The UI still showed the store name, but the session shape is inconsistent.
The admin notify email is awaited inside the public request (adds about 1-2s of latency). Consider a BackgroundTask.

A malformed or expired link returns 401 'Invalid sign-in token' / 'Session expired — sign in again'. This copy is shown to the shop on the review and set-password pages, which is confusing because they are not signing in.

issues: The store chip picker lists every merchant. The DB has 18 leftover merchants named 'TEST_Store' from earlier iterations that can't be told apart, so the admin can't tell which store they are emailing. Consider cleaning up that data and/or showing the email or id on the chip.
The toast overlays the 'WAITING · n' section header for 3s. This is minor.
Placeholders such as 'Mission Bakery Co.' and 'Ana Lopez' look like prefilled values (muted grey on light grey). Consider lighter or example-style placeholders.

action_items: HIGH: make admin notification emails deliverable. For example, route notify_admin through demo_inbox()/TEST_INBOX when the address is the seeded admin@dashlocal.app, or set ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL=delivered@resend.dev in backend/.env for preview. Then verify that the backend log shows 202 for the 'New shop sign-up request' email.
Exclude pw_nonce from GET /api/admin/merchant-accounts and from current_user/auth_me projections.
Optional: show friendlier link-error copy on /review and /set-password, add merchant_name to the set-password response, and send notify_admin in the background.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3844 lines; consider splitting the auth, email and review/signup sections into modules.

The signup rate limit counts only inserted docs per IP. Duplicate or existing-email requests are not counted, which is fine, but declined requests from the same IP still count, so behaviour is acceptable.
submit_review is race-safe (conditional update on status 'sent' before inserting the testimonial). Good.
Purpose-scoped JWTs (review/setpw) are correctly rejected as session tokens, and the setpw nonce is unset after use. Good.

success_rate.backend: 100% of tests (31/31); admin email notification feature failing at the provider

seed_data_creation: Created and then deleted: TEST_ signup_requests, merchant mer-7000b0d8 and user test+uiapprove@resend.dev, the pytest approval merchant/user, all review_requests and testimonials. db.testimonials is empty, GET /api/testimonials returns [], and no drv/trk login_attempts remain. The merchant count is back to 20 (pre-existing).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run tests/test_signup_review_requests.py with -n0. It reads the DB directly (pymongo) and mints review/setpw JWTs with JWT_SECRET. Its module fixture deletes TEST_ signup requests, their merchants and users, all review_requests and testimonials, and drv/trk login_attempts. The signup limit is 5 per IP per hour based on existing docs, so delete TEST_ signup_requests before UI signup tests. The browser_automation sandbox has no pymongo: mint tokens beforehand with tests/mint_ui_tokens_iter24.py [email]. Toasts last 3.2s. 18 old 'TEST_Store' merchants exist from earlier iterations.
rca_of_issue: The admin notify email fails because ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@dashlocal.app is not a real or allowed inbox, so the Emergent email provider blocks it as undeliverable_recipient (422). notify_admin swallows the error and only logs a warning, so the API still returns ok. To reproduce: POST /api/signup-requests, then grep 'Admin notify failed' in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. To fix: send to the test inbox (delivered@resend.dev) for preview, or to a real admin inbox via ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL.
